title: Investigation Apricot: An investigation into alleged corrupt conduct at the Parole Board Queensland

summary.label: Generated summary: written by an AI model from the report text and checked against the cited pages.

sentences.text: Queensland’s Crime and Corruption Commission investigated conduct at Parole Board Queensland, including allegations involving its former president and the former corrective services minister.
The CCC identified weaknesses in governance, staffing, recordkeeping and performance reporting, including unclear authority over board members’ entitlements.
sentences.section: Corruption risks identified through the investigation

sentences.text: The CCC reported that the former president received no education allowance money beyond his entitlement and that the former minister obtained appropriate advice before accepting his resignation.
It made 17 recommendations directly to the board, its secretariat and Queensland Corrective Services about governance, training, appointments, records and reporting.
The CCC also recommended stronger internal controls across public entities and a government review of how entities and their secretariats are established.

items.quote: The lack of governance, policies and a clear demarcation of roles and responsibilities put both the PBQ and the PBQS at risk of fraud and maladministration.

The CCC recommends that all public sector and public service entities have appropriate internal controls and governance frameworks in place to ensure probity, transparency and accountability in their day-to-day operations and decision-making about the use of public funds.
